question: Does gridiron's --seed flag do anything, and what is the noise floor?
why_this_did_not_exist_before: SEED was a module constant with no flag. vector-gridiron 56d8e4e added --seed and threaded it into train_rookie_model, VERIFIED BY INSPECTION AND --help ONLY because the trainer writes assets/ in a repo whose assets/ is mid-operator-decision. This is that deferred check.
how_it_was_run: 3 seeds in an ISOLATED COPY at a scratch path, --offline --skip-build. The 551 MB pipeline/cache was copied too, not junctioned. Real assets checksummed before and after: kdst.json 301817045c3fe765 and nextgame.json 2a50f9529d6eeb87, IDENTICAL both times. UNTOUCHED.

flag_is_not_vacuous.note: The five identical ones are seeded into the copy from the real repo and are not rewritten by train_mtnn.py under --skip-build, so their being identical is not evidence about the seed either way.

FINDING_the_redeploy_baseline_is_one_luc.what_seeds_11_and_13_would_do: FAIL. 62.35 and 61.70 are both below the 63.16 baseline, so a re-run at any seed but 7 is refused redeploy for reasons that are entirely which seed ran.
FINDING_the_redeploy_baseline_is_one_luc.why_this_matters: The baseline is not a property of the model, it is the CQS of one draw. With a CQS seed sd near 0.73 and a gate of '>= baseline' where the baseline IS the high draw, roughly two thirds of honest re-runs are rejected. This is the same shape as the hoops promotion_gate_is_unsatisfiable finding: a threshold set from a single observation of a noisy quantity.
FINDING_the_redeploy_baseline_is_one_luc.promote_bar_vs_observed_max: 63.66 is ABOVE all three seeds, so the promote gate did not fire on any of them either.

what_is_actually_stable: The headline next-game claim is robust. MAE 4.295 / 4.294 / 4.306 across seeds, range 0.012, against a last-4 baseline of 4.616 -- the 'beats by 0.321' margin is 26x the seed range. R2 0.422 / 0.411 / 0.406 and rookie val MAE 2.907 / 2.909 / 2.906 are likewise tight. CQS is the noisy one, and CQS is what the gates use.
LIMITATION_three_seeds: An sd from n=3 is itself very uncertain -- the 95% CI on a 3-sample sd spans roughly 0.5x to 2.8x the estimate. 0.73 is an order-of-magnitude statement, not a floor to size experiments against. Do not compute a paired MDE from it and quote the result as though it were the pitch floor (5 seeds) or the hoops floor. Three seeds establishes NON-VACUITY of the flag and shows the baseline problem; it does not establish a measurement floor.
